name: The Shins
label: Sub Pop
lede: A side project from an Albuquerque basement ended up in a McDonald's ad, a Natalie Portman scene and No. 2 on the Billboard 200. Then James Mercer rebuilt the band around himself.

eras.title: Albuquerque, a basement and a side project
eras.text: James Mercer spent the '90s in Flake Music, a four-piece in a city nobody's A&R reps visited. The Shins started as his side project, and by 2000 it was the only thing he cared about.

years.h: Four Albuquerque friends start Flake Music
years.p: James Mercer, Jesse Sandoval, Marty Crandall and Neal Langford put out the Spork EP and an album for Omnibus Records, and tour with [[Modest Mouse|a96ac800-bfcb-412a-8a63-0a98df600700]] and [[Califone|68025033-de1b-42f5-8a21-bedfb8895dda]].
years.xp: Flake Music's album was When You Land Here, It's Time to Return. It was reissued in November 2014.

years.h: While Flake Music plays on, Mercer starts The Shins
years.p: Mercer and drummer Sandoval open as a two-piece for Cibo Matto and [[The American Analog Set|7f5dde96-1573-4491-9673-f03fe7c5caaa]]. Unlike Flake Music, Mercer writes everything.

years.h: Nature Bears a Vacuum is the first Shins 7-inch
years.p: Omnibus Records puts out the single. A second, When I Goose-Step, follows, then a tour with [[Modest Mouse|a96ac800-bfcb-412a-8a63-0a98df600700]].

years.h: Flake Music breaks up and the lineup fills out
years.p: Bassist Neal Langford and keyboardist Marty Crandall move over to The Shins. Early members Dave Hernandez and Ron Skrasek go back to their band Scared of Chaka.

years.h: Isaac Brock mails Mercer's cassette demos to labels
years.p: Mercer is stuck in Albuquerque, obsessing over a debut album. [[Isaac Brock|071d3d16-8ed7-4e06-be96-2c52defcf434]] of Modest Mouse and Zeke Howard of [[Love as Laughter|8f5c6093-27ba-402d-b092-4157c93a4104]] pass his tapes around.

eras.title: One single, then a hamburger ad
eras.text: A one-off Sub Pop single turned into a record deal, and a record made in a basement turned into the indie album of the moment. Then McDonald's paid for "New Slang," and the band's hometown alt-weekly didn't like it.

years.big: "All of a sudden my whole life was up in smoke."
years.h: Jonathan Poneman hears the band open for Modest Mouse and makes an offer
years.p: Sub Pop co-founder Jonathan Poneman offers a one-off single after a San Francisco show. That's James Mercer on what the next months did to him.
years.xp:
"New Slang" went out to the Sub Pop Singles Club in February 2001, and Sub Pop signed the band.

Mercer's life turned over at once: he signed, quit his job, left town, and a five-year relationship ended.

years.h: Oh, Inverted World arrives, mostly recorded in a basement
years.p: Most of The Shins' debut was recorded in Mercer's basement before Sub Pop ever called. Critics hear '60s pop through a skewed lens, and Albuquerque suddenly has a band people talk about.
years.xp: The album was recorded across 2000 and 2001 and came out on June 19, 2001. Mercer says his favorite is the closer, The Past and Pending, because it works on him more than the others.

years.h: McDonald's puts "New Slang" in a Winter Olympics ad
years.p: James Mercer licenses the song for the 2002 commercial. Indie fans and Albuquerque's alt-weekly cry foul.
years.xp: Mercer has been upfront about it: he told The New York Times he made more money from touring and licensing than from record sales. The cash let him buy a house and move to Portland, Oregon.

years.h: Langford is out before Chutes Too Narrow
years.p: Dave Hernandez takes over on bass. Jesse Sandoval told The Guardian in 2009 that Langford didn't leave, he was fired.

years.h: Burglars take the Oh, Inverted World masters from Mercer's house
years.p: Thieves walk off with the HP Pavilion holding the mastered files. DAT backups at the mastering house save the album, but it can never be remixed, except "New Slang," which survived on a DVD.

years.h: Chutes Too Narrow gets a Portland basement for a studio
years.p: The Shins record their second album themselves, cheaper than a real studio and not comfortable. It reaches No. 86 on the Billboard 200.

eras.title: A movie scene, a leak and No. 2
eras.text: One scene in a small indie film did more for The Shins than any review. Within three years the band went from No. 86 to No. 2 on the Billboard 200, and Sub Pop had its biggest chart week ever.

years.h: A movie scene turns "New Slang" into a life-changer
years.p: In Zach Braff's Garden State, Natalie Portman's character hands his character her headphones and promises the song will change his life. For The Shins, it does.
years.xp:
Caring Is Creepy is in the film too. Sales of both Shins albums more than doubled, colleges wanted them on campus, and Spin wrote that they became indie-rock icons almost overnight. Some early fans felt the obscurity had been part of the point.

Oh, Inverted World went on to sell 500,000 copies in the U.S.

years.h: Mercer can't sleep, so he works until dawn
years.p: Late in 2005 James Mercer gets up in the middle of the night and works in his home studio. The album's title and its opener, Sleeping Lessons, both point at it.
years.xp: Rolling Stone reported that the title refers to Mercer's crippling insomnia. Sleeping Lessons was at one point considered as the album title.

years.h: Three months early, Wincing the Night Away leaks
years.p: A promo copy of the third album hits the internet in October. The single Phantom Limb follows officially on November 14.

years.h: iTunes sells Wincing the Night Away two weeks early, by mistake
years.p: For a day, the album is for sale on iTunes, two weeks before its street date. It's pulled the next day.

years.h: Ten days before release, The Shins play Saturday Night Live
years.p: Jake Gyllenhaal hosts, and The Shins are the musical guest.

years.h: Wincing the Night Away lands at No. 2, higher than Sub Pop has ever been
years.p: Produced by James Mercer and [[Joe Chiccarelli|2a250f44-5473-4dc9-a8ba-2320fb31b2f9]], it sells more than 118,000 copies in week one. No Sub Pop record had ever charted that high on the Billboard 200.
years.xp:
It was made in three places: Mercer's basement studio in Oregon City, [[Phil Ek|974863b2-1c82-4bb7-b23f-54ddf2713e88]]'s home in Seattle, and a Portland studio. It topped the digital, rock, independent and Tastemakers charts the same week, then fell to No. 8 in week two on about 53,000 copies.

Metacritic scores it 79 out of 100. Mercer has said it came out of a painful breakup and the band's sudden fame.

eras.title: Mercer clears the room
eras.text: After a Grammy nod, Mercer was tired of being the center of everything. He left Sub Pop, made a record with Danger Mouse, and parted with every other Shin.

years.h: A Grammy nomination, and no win
years.p: Wincing the Night Away is up for Best Alternative Music Album in February. The Shins don't win.

q: Jesse Sandoval, to the Portland Mercury
years.h: Sandoval says fired. Mercer says an aesthetic decision.
years.p: James Mercer parts with every other Shin: Jesse Sandoval, Marty Crandall and Dave Hernandez. [[Joe Plummer|5fd1bd8e-f2b4-4f01-acc0-3423456f06ae]] of Modest Mouse takes over the drums.
years.xp:
Mercer said he was "tired of being right in the middle and everything sort of revolving around me." He said he'd always loved auteurs who presented themselves as bands, like Neutral Milk Hotel and Lilys, and called the change tremendously difficult.

Sandoval, there from the start, told the Portland Mercury he was fired. Mercer also moved The Shins off Sub Pop to his own label, Aural Apothecary.

years.h: Danger Mouse knocks, and Broken Bells follows
years.p: Producer Brian Burton, known as [[Danger Mouse|4b356f05-bcc2-4544-925b-fd9a1bf708be]], approaches James Mercer, and the two make music as [[Broken Bells|62d364d2-550b-420e-b918-b3bd1e4a2efc]]. Mercer likes working with new people so much he wants that feeling in The Shins too.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the project helped Mercer overcome his fears of collaboration.

years.cap: The Shins at DeLuna Fest, Pensacola, October 15, 2011
years.h: Yuuki Matthews, Jessica Dobson and Richard Swift become the new Shins
years.p: James Mercer rebuilds with bassist Matthews of Crystal Skulls, guitarist [[Jessica Dobson|24d03776-9bfc-4bcf-b52f-bd316e5f9ee9]] and multi-instrumentalist [[Richard Swift|dd5f8909-245d-458b-833a-cd6b698399ce]]. Joe Plummer stays on drums.

eras.title: New band, same name
eras.text: The rebuilt Shins debuted at No. 3 and landed the band's biggest radio hit. Mercer then steered back toward the old sound on Heartworms, and the band lost Richard Swift.

years.h: Port of Morrow debuts at No. 3
years.p: Produced with [[Greg Kurstin|ef2a8c11-a35a-4c61-b750-5cb29c1223f4]], who pushes James Mercer to experiment. Simple Song becomes The Shins' biggest hit, reaching the top 10 of Billboard's Alternative Songs chart.

years.cap: The Shins at ACL Live, Austin, March 18, 2012
years.h: Austin City Limits films the rebuilt Shins
years.p: The new lineup plays an episode of the show the month Port of Morrow comes out.

years.h: Zach Braff calls again, this time for Wish I Was Here
years.p: Ten years after Garden State, The Shins record "So Now What" for Braff's film. James Mercer tells Billboard it's one of the best things he's ever done.

years.h: The Shins cover the Beatles for a kids' cartoon
years.p: They record "The Word" for Netflix's animated series Beat Bugs, built on Beatles songs.

years.h: Heartworms goes back to the old Shins sounds
years.p: James Mercer says he made a deliberate effort to use the sounds he'd used historically for the band.
years.xp: In January 2018 came The Worm's Heart, a reimagined version of the whole album.

years.h: Richard Swift dies at 41
years.p: Swift, who played in The Shins from 2011 to 2016, dies in Tacoma, Washington. His family says the cause was complications from hepatitis plus liver and kidney distress, and that he'd struggled with alcohol addiction all his life.
years.xp: Swift played keys, bass, guitar and much more in The Shins, toured as The Black Keys' bassist in 2014 and 2015, and made his own records for Secretly Canadian. Fleet Foxes' Robin Pecknold later named him in the song Sunblind.

eras.title: Twenty-one candles for Oh, Inverted World
eras.text: The Shins spent the early 2020s going back to where it started: a remaster, a tour of the first album start to finish, a platinum plaque, and the loss of the bassist who played on it.

years.h: The Shins return with "The Great Divide"
years.p: It's their first new song since Heartworms.

years.h: Bob Ludwig remasters Oh, Inverted World for its 20th birthday
years.p: Sub Pop's anniversary reissue is remastered by Ludwig with James Mercer assisting, in new artwork and packaging.

yt: Full show, Oh, Inverted World 21st Birthday Tour
years.h: Oh, Inverted World, front to back, on the road
years.p: Announced in May 2022, the 21st Birthday tour plays The Shins' debut in full across North America.

years.h: Oh, Inverted World goes platinum, 22 years on
years.p: The RIAA certifies the debut in May, making it the third Sub Pop album to get there, after Nirvana's Bleach and The Postal Service's Give Up.

years.h: Original Shins bassist Neal Langford dies at 50
years.p: Langford, who played in Flake Music and on Oh, Inverted World, dies in July. No cause was reported. James Mercer says Langford talked him out of his shyness and into the microphone.
years.xp: After The Shins, Langford and Marty Crandall made an EP as Sad Baby Wolf in 2013. He had been living in North Carolina with his partner.

years.h: Mercer says the next project is a new Shins album
years.p: James Mercer tells Consequence his next project is a new Shins record.
